report.answer_text:
GPT‑5 is an AI model family that OpenAI released on August 7, 2025. It became the default in ChatGPT at launch. Its biggest change was that ChatGPT could automatically choose between a fast model for everyday questions and a deeper reasoning model, GPT‑5 Thinking, for harder tasks. (openai.com)
Its main improvements were:
Better coding and tool use. GPT‑5 was better at writing and debugging code, working with existing codebases, and using tools across multi-step tasks. (openai.com)
Stronger reasoning and image understanding. It improved on tasks involving math, science, and visual inputs such as charts and diagrams. It also improved at writing and following detailed instructions. (openai.com)
More reliable answers. OpenAI reported fewer factual errors and less tendency to agree with users just to please them. It could still make mistakes. (openai.com)
More control for developers. The API launched with GPT‑5, GPT‑5 mini, and GPT‑5 nano, plus settings for how much reasoning the model does and how detailed its answers are. (openai.com)

quotes.text: GPT‑5 is the new default in ChatGPT, replacing GPT‑4o, OpenAI o3, OpenAI o4-mini, GPT‑4.1, and GPT‑4.5 for signed-in users.
GPT‑5 is starting to roll out today to all Plus, Pro, Team, and Free users, with access for Enterprise and Edu coming next week.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes state GPT-5 is the new default in ChatGPT and that it began rolling out today to Plus, Pro, Team, and Free users, which backs the main point, but they do not explicitly say it was the default at launch for Enterprise and Edu users, who got access later.
pages.page_reason: The page says GPT‑5 is the new default in ChatGPT for signed-in users and that its rollout began that day.

quotes.text: GPT‑5 is a unified system with a smart, efficient model that answers most questions, a deeper reasoning model (GPT‑5 thinking) for harder problems, and a real‑time router that quickly decides which to use based on conversation type, complexity, tool needs, and your explicit intent

GPT‑5 is the new default in ChatGPT, replacing GPT‑4o, OpenAI o3, OpenAI o4-mini, GPT‑4.1, and GPT‑4.5 for signed-in users. Just open ChatGPT and type your question; GPT‑5 handles the rest, applying reasoning automatically when the response would benefit from it.

pages.page_reason: The page says GPT‑5 uses a router to choose between an efficient model for most questions and GPT‑5 Thinking for harder problems, but it does not call this GPT‑5’s biggest change.

quotes.text: GPT‑5 is state-of-the-art (SOTA) across key coding benchmarks, scoring 74.9% on SWE-bench Verified and 88% on Aider polyglot.
It excels at producing high-quality code and handling tasks such as fixing bugs, editing code, and answering questions about complex codebases.
We’ve also found GPT‑5 to be excellent at digging deep into codebases to answer questions about how various pieces work or interoperate.

GPT‑5’s improved tool intelligence lets it reliably chain together dozens of tool calls—both in sequence and in parallel—without losing its way, making it far better at executing complex, real-world tasks end to end.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes state GPT-5 excels at producing and debugging code (fixing bugs, editing code), at answering questions about complex codebases, and at chaining dozens of tool calls across multi-step, end-to-end tasks, which covers every part of the claim.
pages.page_reason: The page says GPT‑5 produces high-quality code, fixes bugs, handles questions about complex codebases, and reliably chains tool calls to complete complex tasks.

quotes.text: It sets a new state of the art across math (94.6% on AIME 2025 without tools)
including state-of-the-art performance on GPQA, which contains extremely difficult science questions.
The model excels across a range of multimodal benchmarks, spanning visual, video-based, spatial, and scientific reasoning.

Stronger multimodal performance means ChatGPT can reason more accurately over images and other non-text inputs—whether that’s interpreting a chart, summarizing a photo of a presentation, or answering questions about a diagram.
